message.content:
Yes—if you’re experiencing excessive or disruptive noise in Atlanta, you can file a complaint with the city’s authorities. In the United States, “local council” usually refers to the city council, but noise complaints are typically handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** or the **City Code Enforcement** office. Here’s how you can do it:

---

## 1. Contact the City of Atlanta Police Department

| Method | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Phone** | 311 (for non-emergency services) or 404‑656‑3111 (Atlanta Police Department) |
| **Online** | Use the City of Atlanta’s online portal: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| **In‑person** | Visit the nearest police precinct or the City Hall at 55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303 |

### What to Provide
- **Your name and contact information** (so the department can follow up).
- **Location of the noise** (street address or intersection).
- **Time and duration** of the disturbance.
- **Description of the noise** (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs).
- **Any relevant evidence** (photos, videos, audio recordings).

---

## 2. Use the City of Atlanta Online Complaint Form

1. Go to the **311 portal**: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311>.
2. Select **“Noise Complaint”** from the list of service requests.
3. Fill out the required fields (location, time, description, etc.).
4. Attach any supporting documents or media files.
5. Submit the form; you’ll receive a confirmation number and an estimated response time.

---

## 3. Check the Noise Ordinance

Atlanta’s noise ordinance (Title 10, Chapter 1 of the Atlanta Municipal Code) sets limits on permissible noise levels and defines quiet hours (generally 10 p.m.–7 a.m.). Knowing the specific regulations can help you describe the violation accurately.

- **Quiet Hours**: 10 p.m.–7 a.m. (except for certain permitted activities like construction during daylight hours).
- **Allowed Noise Levels**: Typically measured in decibels (dB); the city may have specific thresholds for residential vs. commercial areas.

You can view the full ordinance here: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/city-code-enforcement/noise-ordinance>.

---

## 4. Follow Up

- If you don’t receive a response within a few days, call 311 or the police department again using your confirmation number.
- For ongoing or repeated disturbances, you may request a formal investigation or a citation.

---

## Quick Reference

| Resource | Link | Contact |
|----------|------|---------|
| City of Atlanta 311 Portal | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> | 311 |
| Atlanta Police Department | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/police> | 404‑656‑3111 |
| Noise Ordinance | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/city-code-enforcement/noise-ordinance> | 404‑656‑3111 |
| City Hall | 55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303 | 404‑656‑3111 |

---

### Bottom Line

Yes, you can report a noise complaint to the City of Atlanta. Use the 311 system, the online portal, or call the police department directly. Provide as much detail as possible, and reference the city’s noise ordinance to strengthen your case. The city will investigate and take appropriate action—often issuing a warning or citation if the noise violates local regulations.
